clinician.trajectory_summary: A 6-year-old patient presented with sudden decrease in vision in the right eye following blunt trauma. Initial examination revealed hyphema, corneal edema, post-traumatic uveitis, and a diminished red reflex. Indirect fundoscopy and Optical Coherence Tomography (OCT) confirmed a full-thickness macular rupture. The patient underwent pars plana vitrectomy (PPV) with internal limiting membrane (ILM) peeling using the inverted flap technique and 20% SF6 gas tamponade. Three months postoperatively, OCT imaging showed a closed macular defect and residual tissue reorganization, with best-corrected visual acuity improving to 0.3.
